{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KgdWfiDuJ9sDs7VcyuGAUc","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\"\"\"Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.\n\nResponsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,\nnormalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n\n    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    node: Text | None\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    original_length: int\n    can_open: bool\n    can_close: bool\n    active: bool = True\n    previous: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    next: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on runs of equal length.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. Everything else is\n    escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                html, index = code_span\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index:run_end]))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                html, index = autolink\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                out.append(raw[index:raw_html_end])\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                out.append(escape_html(value))\n                continue\n        out.append(escape_html(char))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":6,"oldLines":10,"newStart":6,"newLines":59,"lines":[" \"\"\""," "," import re","+import unicodedata","+from dataclasses import dataclass, field"," "," from mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference"," from mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url"," ","+# Inline nodes. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"","+","+    tag: str","+    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)","+","+","+Node = Text | Html | Element","+","+","+@dataclass(eq=False)","+class Delimiter:","+    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Leftover delimiter runs are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.html)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n        else:\n            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start + 1\n    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n\n    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong elements (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n            )\n            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n                return potential\n Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n        if entry.next is not None:\n            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n        else:\n            self.top = entry.previous\n\n    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n        opener.next = closer\n        closer.previous = opener\n\n    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(entry)\n        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n\n    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n\n    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the nodes between the opener and closer into a new element placed after the opener.\"\"\"\n        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n\n    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n            if candidate is node:\n                return index\n        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# Inline nodes. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n\n    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    node: Text | None\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    original_length: int\n    can_open: bool\n    can_close: bool\n    active: bool = True\n    previous: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    next: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on runs of equal length.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. Everything else is\n    escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                html, index = code_span\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index:run_end]))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                html, index = autolink\n                out.append(html)\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                out.append(raw[index:raw_html_end])\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            out.append(escape_html(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                out.append(escape_html(value))\n                continue\n        out.append(escape_html(char))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":108,"oldLines":10,"newStart":108,"newLines":12,"lines":["     same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. word + mark + \"\\n\")\n        stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert stdout.count(\"<strong>\") == 1\n        assert stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_intraword_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-intraword-rules: intraword emphasis works with star but not with underscore.\"\"\"\n    star = run_executable(project_root, \"foo*bar*baz\\n\")\n    under = run_executable(project_root, \"foo_bar_baz\\n\")\n    assert star.returncode == 0\n    assert under.returncode == 0\n    assert star.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 1\n    assert under.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_flanking_whitespace(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-flanking-whitespace: a run followed or preceded by whitespace does not emphasize.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"a * foo bar*\\n\\nfoo bar *\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_nesting(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-nesting: triple delimiters give one em and one strong; nested forms keep both.\"\"\"\n    triple = run_executable(project_root, \"***word***\\n\")\n    nested = run_executable(project_root, \"*a **b** c*\\n\")\n    assert triple.returncode == 0\n    assert nested.returncode == 0\n    assert triple.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 1\n    assert triple.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<strong>\") == 1\n    assert nested.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 1\n    assert nested.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<strong>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_code_span_binds_tighter(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-code-span-binds-tighter: a star inside a code span cannot close emphasis.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"*foo`*`\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<code>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Single and doubled delimiters ---\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_single_star_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A single star pair wraps its word in one em element.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"*wordy*\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\") == \"<p><em>wordy</em></p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_single_underscore_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A single underscore pair wraps its word in test_emphasis_double_star_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A doubled star pair wraps its word in one strong element.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"**wordy**\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\") == \"<p><strong>wordy</strong></p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_double_underscore_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A doubled underscore pair wraps test_emphasis_triple_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Triple stars give em outside strong, following the length-matching rule.\"\"\"\n    assert inlines.parse_inline(\"***word***\") == {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1eaxS4pVVodXbg9Hu6e","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01KLWKmR4kWkgnGSkimwQ4Kz","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'\ndef edit(path, pairs):\n    src = open(path, encoding=\"utf-8\").read()\n    for old, new in pairs:\n        assert src.count(old) == 1, old\n        src = src.replace(old, new)\n    open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\").write(src)\n\nedit(\"tests/test_emphasis.py\", [\n    ('\"\"\"AC emphasis-flanking-whitespace: a run followed or preceded by whitespace does not emphasize.\"\"\"',\n     '\"\"\"AC emphasis-flanking-whitespace: a run next to whitespace does not form emphasis.\"\"\"'),\n    ('\"\"\"Both-flanking runs whose lengths sum to a multiple of 3 do not pair unless both are multiples of 3.\"\"\"',\n     '\"\"\"Both-flanking runs whose lengths sum to a multiple of 3 do not pair (rule of 3).\"\"\"'),\n    ('\"\"\"Delimiter stacks do not carry across paragraphs, so an opener in one paragraph does not pair.\"\"\"',\n     '\"\"\"Delimiter stacks do not carry across paragraphs, so an opener cannot pair across them.\"\"\"'),\n    ('''def test_emphasis_closer_pairs_with_nearest_opener() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A closer pairs with the nearest eligible opener, not the first one in the paragraph.\"\"\"\n    assert inlines.parse_inline(\"*a *b* c*\") == \"*a <em>b</em> c*\"''',\n     '''def test_emphasis_closer_pairs_with_nearest_opener() -> None:\n    \"\"\"The inner closer pairs with the nearest opener, then the outer closer pairs with the first.\"\"\"\n    assert inlines.parse_inline(\"*a *b* c*\") == \"<em>a <em>b</em> c</em>\"'''),\n])\nedit(\"mdparser/inlines.py\", [\n    ('# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. The remaining tests compare the executable's stdout bytes or a returned string with its\nexact expected value.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom mdparser import inlines\n\n\ndef run_executable(project_root: Path, data: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=data.encode(\"utf-8\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Emphasis.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_star_and_underscore(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-star-and-underscore: single star and single underscore wrap a word in one em.\"\"\"\n    word = \"wordy\"\n    for mark in (\"*\", \"_\"):\n        result = run_executable(project_root, mark + word + mark + \"\\n\")\n        stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n        assert stdout.count(\"<strong>\") == 0\n        assert word in stdout\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_strong(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-strong: doubled delimiters produce one strong element.\"\"\"\n    word = \"wordy\"\n    for mark in (\"**\", \"__\"):\n        result = run_executable(project_root, mark + word + mark + \"\\n\")\n        stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert stdout.count(\"<strong>\") == 1\n        assert stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_intraword_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-intraword-rules: intraword emphasis works with star but not with underscore.\"\"\"\n    star = run_executable(project_root, \"foo*bar*baz\\n\")\n    under = run_executable(project_root, \"foo_bar_baz\\n\")\n    assert star.returncode == 0\n    assert under.returncode == 0\n    assert star.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 1\n    assert under.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_flanking_whitespace(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-flanking-whitespace: a run followed or preceded by whitespace does not emphasize.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"a * foo bar*\\n\\nfoo bar *\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_nesting(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-nesting: triple delimiters give one em and one strong; nested forms keep both.\"\"\"\n    triple = run_executable(project_root, \"***word***\\n\")\n    nested = run_executable(project_root, \"*a **b** c*\\n\")\n    assert triple.returncode == 0\n    assert nested.returncode == 0\n    assert triple.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 1\n    assert triple.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<strong>\") == 1\n    assert nested.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 1\n    assert nested.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<strong>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_code_span_binds_tighter(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC emphasis-code-span-binds-tighter: a star inside a code span cannot close emphasis.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"*foo`*`\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<em>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<code>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Single and doubled delimiters ---\n\n\ndef {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1epK6du5GoVeVvPUTcy","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"RESULT: SUCCESS\n\nFILES CHANGED:\n- mdparser/inlines.py\n- tests/test_emphasis.py\n\nSUMMARY:\n- `parse_inline` now builds a node list instead of joining strings. Code spans, autolinks, raw HTML, escapes and entities are `Html` nodes. Each `*` or `_` run is a `Text` node pushed on a `DelimiterStack`, with `can_open`/`can_close` set from the flanking rules.\n- Flanking uses `unicodedata`: Unicode whitespace is tab, LF, FF, CR or Zs, and the line edges count as whitespace. It uses a doubly linked stack with a bottom sentinel, `openers_bottom` per character, closer length mod 3 and closer-can-open, the multiple-of-3 rule, and strong versus em selection. Unmatched runs stay as escaped literal text. Wrapping moves the nodes between a matched pair into an `Element`.\n- Tests: `tests/test_emphasis.py` (40 tests). The six declared acceptance checks are transcribed with their assertions unchanged. The rest check exact output for single and double delimiters, triple and nested runs, flanking, the rule of 3, unmatched and empty runs, and code-span interaction.\n- Results: `python3 -m pytest -q` gives 459 passed, 0 failed. That is the existing 419 plus 40 new.\n- I did not run `sh sources/full_test.sh`. The corpus section for Emphasis needs links, so the spec gates it in the images story.\n\nChoices I made that you may want to redirect:\n- `openers_bottom` is keyed by the closer's original length mod 3, not the current length. The spec says \"length\"; the rule of 3 depends on original lengths.\n- The stack operates on a sibling node list passed in at construction.
